correctness.rationale: Exact residual projector identity holds because A=I_2; the rank-one Rayleigh maximum leaves the squared smaller singular value. The centered case rotates signed coordinate sums into independent fair walks, giving alpha^2(D-m_D^2)/(2D^2). The one-sided binomial case yields alpha^2[1/4+1/(4D)-m_D/(2D)]. Walk absolute moments follow from a telescoping probability-of-zero recurrence; Stirling gives limits. D=1, D=2, SPD bounds, and strict D>=2 positivity are proved. Standalone exact rational tests confirm finitely many cases but are not used to infer all D.

value.rationale: The source problem explicitly balances independently programmed analog copies against the rank of a digital residual correction. This complete two-regime exact minimal model shows raw programming MSE strictly decreases while the optimal corrected risk jumps from zero to positive at D=2; centered copies recover order 1/D but persistent one-sided bias leaves a sharp alpha^2/4 floor. Quantifying the two distinct regimes offers a mathematically motivated configuration test, not a tiny arbitrary numerical parameter perturbation.
